Although Apple has always positioned privacy as a selling point for its hardware and services, I sometimes wonder whether it now regrets one privacy measure it introduced — App Tracking Transparency (ATT).

Such a limited-scope measure seems to face a new antitrust lawsuit or regulatory challenge every few months. A third lawsuit against ATT has been filed in the UK, and this time there is something particularly noteworthy.

This article has been updated, with Apple's response appended at the end...

Personalised Advertising Controversy

Personalised advertising has long been one of the most controversial topics in the tech industry. The ads we see are no longer random products we may or may not be interested in, but are tailored based on our interests — collected through the apps we use and the websites we browse.

In theory, this is a win-win situation for everyone. Consumers see ads they may genuinely be interested in; advertisers get better return on investment because the ads are more targeted; and ad-funded free apps and websites generate higher revenue for the same reason.

Although the data used to serve personalised ads is collected anonymously, the practice is widely regarded as an invasion of privacy. Even though Apple developed a technology specifically to ensure data anonymity, many consumers remain wary of it.

App Tracking Transparency

Apple's App Tracking Transparency is designed to address this issue by letting consumers choose whether their data can be used to serve personalised ads. Developers who wish to collect such data must first obtain the consumer's consent.

However, for the iPhone maker, this move has triggered a series of lawsuits and antitrust investigations — primarily because Apple's own apps are not required to seek such consent. Apple has repeatedly stressed that its rules are in fact consistent: its own apps do not display the ATT prompt because they do not collect the data covered by the prompt. Third-party apps that also do not collect such data are similarly exempt from having to display the prompt.

Latest UK Lawsuit

Apple has so far faced three complaints before the UK's relevant antitrust regulator — the Competition Appeal Tribunal. It lost the first lawsuit (currently under appeal), while the second is still ongoing.

Reuters reported the third lawsuit filed today.

What's Special About It

The latest lawsuit has an interesting twist: it was brought by Ann Pope, a former senior official of the regulator overseeing this case.

Ann Pope, a former senior official of the UK's Competition and Markets Authority, is leading the lawsuit. She said Apple's policies "have caused very serious harm to businesses that rely on Apple as a gatekeeper." Pope stated in a declaration: "This lawsuit is essential to protecting the rights of UK businesses that depend on Apple, ensuring that the rules Apple implements are fair, and compensating UK companies for the losses they have suffered."

Following an investigation by the German antitrust authority, Apple recently agreed to make eight changes to its ATT rules in the EU. Regarding this lawsuit, Apple told us:

Over the years, many privacy advocates have publicly voiced support for ATT.
